explain: Product success is measured against a non-AI baseline on the same user task. Generated text is useful only if it improves the relevant outcome without breaking constraints.
steps: Compare completion time and supported-answer rate under the same fixture. || Require the support target before accepting the faster variant.
name: user-baseline

explain: A task reserves shared budget before expensive work and returns unused funds afterward. This arithmetic model needs atomic durable enforcement across real replicas.
steps: Compare the reservation with available budget. || Refuse the second reservation when it would exceed the remaining allowance.
name: quota-reservation

explain: Upload, extraction, indexing, and active search visibility are distinct states. Receiving all file bytes does not establish that a document is searchable.
steps: Store preparation stages separately from publication. || Display indexing status until a complete generation has been activated.
name: lifecycle-progress

explain: End-to-end checks compare visible UI outcomes with authoritative records. A completed screen with no committed result is a contract failure even if text generation succeeded.
steps: Record the screen's terminal state and the effect ledger independently. || Require them to agree on the operation identity.
name: end-to-end-evidence

explain: A completion artifact checklist turns a learning claim into reviewable work. Missing recovery evidence keeps the topic incomplete even when a demo exists.
steps: Declare explanation, implementation, failure reproduction, and trade-off evidence. || Report the missing artifact instead of equating a learned flag with competence.
name: capstone-artifacts
journey-921
explain: A source-linked reasoning fixture. JSON parsing checks representation only; reproduce the actual mechanism with the chapter reference.
steps: Inspect the declared input and required invariant. || Trace the chapter mechanism and reproduce the stated case. || Change the stated assumption and defend the result.
expect: Reasoning input only; no program result is claimed. Reproduce the scenario using the chapter’s runnable reference.
limit: A JSON case is parsed for representation integrity only, not executed as a proof of its semantic claim.
